service.description: Extract Shopify orders for an automation window through Shopify Bulk Operations and write normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder.

parameter.name: shopifyAuthConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned ShopifyAuthConfig identifier.

parameter.name: automationId
parameter.description: Automation id passed through for metadata.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: fileSide
parameter.description: Logical file side being extracted.

parameter.name: systemEnumId
parameter.description: Source system identifier passed through for metadata.

parameter.name: sourceTypeEnumId
parameter.description: Source type identifier passed through for metadata.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: preserveWindowInstants
parameter.description: When true, treat windowStart and windowEnd as already normalized instants instead of reinterpreting UTC-midnight values through the Shopify config timezone.

parameter.name: windowStartDate
parameter.description: Raw parent window start passed by the automation executor.

parameter.name: windowEndDate
parameter.description: Raw parent window end passed by the automation executor.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to shopify-orders-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id for live extract progress. Accepted for dispatch-contract symmetry with the OMS extractor; Shopify progress emission (bulk-operation objectCount heartbeats) is a planned follow-up.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total for progress percent. Accepted, not yet used.

parameter.name: connectTimeoutMillis
parameter.description: HTTP connect timeout for Shopify GraphQL and Bulk Operations download requests.

parameter.name: readTimeoutMillis
parameter.description: HTTP read timeout for Shopify GraphQL and Bulk Operations download requests.

parameter.name: maxAttempts
parameter.description: Maximum attempts for retryable Shopify GraphQL transport failures.

parameter.name: maxBulkPollAttempts
parameter.description: Maximum Shopify Bulk Operations status polls before the extraction fails.

parameter.name: bulkPollIntervalMillis
parameter.description: Delay between Shopify Bulk Operations status polls.

parameter.name: bulkStartRetryAttempts
parameter.description: Number of retries when Shopify rejects the start request because another Bulk Operation is already running.

parameter.name: bulkStartRetryDelayMillis
parameter.description: Delay between Bulk Operation start retries when another operation is already running.

service.description:
Extract per-EVENT Shopify records for a window, for returns reconciliation against the OMS reconciliationReturns extract (DAR-BE-018). An event is a refund OR a return; this is the second reshape of this service's output — see ShopifyReturnRefsSupport's class doc (2026-08-17 returns-refund-grain-alignment plan, Task 1, REVISION 2026-08-18) for the full shape history.
Uses CURSOR pagination, not Bulk Operations: refunds and returns are GraphQL connections, and the bulk path rejects connection-bearing fields because bulk JSONL emits their children as separate __parentId lines that nothing here re-nests. That is why this service carries no bulk poll/retry parameters.
WINDOW SEMANTICS: this windows on the CREATION of each event itself, not on any order-level date (an order can be arbitrarily older than a refund or return on it). The Shopify search is a wide, lower-bound-only net (updated_at >= windowStart - lookbackHours, no upper bound, trimmed to orders that plausibly carry a refund or a return); [windowStart - lookbackHours, windowEnd) is then applied client-side against each refund's and each return's own createdAt independently. The lookback (default 3h) exists because OMS lags Shopify by ~38min (RQ-23): an OMS row just inside windowStart can point at a Shopify event created just before it, and that event must still be fetched for the OMS-side forward match to see it. See ShopifyReturnRefsSupport for the full rationale.
Each output record is one EVENT: {eventId, eventType, orderId, createdAt}, all ids bare (GID tail stripped) so they land in the same space as the OMS externalId. eventType is "REFUND" or "RETURN". eventId is the single join key OMS reconciliationReturns.externalId matches against — no precedence rule needed: the product owner confirmed (2026-08-18) that externalId is usually a Shopify refund id but sometimes a return id, and emitting both kinds as same-shaped rows under one eventId column means whichever kind OMS actually used, the matching Shopify row is there to join against directly. This revision retires the refundId/returnId column split (and with it the refund-to-return association problem — see ShopifyReturnRefsSupport.toRecords for that investigation's history) and the earlier "no refund yet" warning: a return with no refund yet now emits its own RETURN row rather than being dropped.
REFUNDED-RETURN NARROWING (2026-08-18): a refunded return is represented by its REFUND row ALONE — the return itself does not also get a RETURN row, since the OMS-side contract (one row per return, one externalId field, stamped with the refund id once one exists — see ReturnPresenceVerificationSupport's class doc, "a refunded Shopify Return is never separately expected; its event is its refund") means a refunded return gets exactly ONE OMS counterpart, keyed by the refund id; a separate RETURN row for it would be a permanent, structural phantom missing-in-OMS. The discriminator is Return.refunds (a RefundConnection, confirmed present with no required args on every dated API version this catalog supports — not returns.nodes.status: that field was investigated first and REJECTED, since Shopify's own returnClose mutation doc confirms a return can reach CLOSED with zero refunds, and nothing prevents a refund existing while a return stays OPEN, so status cannot cleanly separate refunded from unrefunded returns in either direction. A return whose Return.refunds connection comes back empty gets its own RETURN row; any non-empty result means it is skipped. See ShopifyReturnRefsSupport.toRecords for the full rationale and evidence.

parameter.name: shopifyAuthConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned Shopify auth config identifier.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to shopify-return-refs-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: pageSize
parameter.description: Orders per cursor page.

parameter.name: connectionPageSize
parameter.description: Refunds/returns fetched per order. Clamped to the ShopifySourceCatalog connectionMaxPageSize (100) regardless of the value requested here; truncation detection reads the clamped value back off the built query, not this raw parameter, so a warning still fires naming the order rather than silently truncating its id set. Also governs the nested per-return Return.refunds existence check (2026-08-18 narrowing) — it shares the same refunds connectionRoot/page-size as the order-level refunds list, since only emptiness of that nested connection is ever read, never its count.

parameter.name: lookbackHours
parameter.description: Hours the fetch/emit floor is widened BEFORE windowStart, so a Shopify event created just before windowStart is still available for the OMS-side forward match (OMS lags Shopify by ~38min, RQ-23). Does not change the reporting window itself — matches ReturnPresenceVerificationSupport.DEFAULT_GRACE_HOURS in the darpan component by default.

service.description: Point-existence check for Shopify order ids against the primary datastore via nodes(ids:). The bulk extraction's orders(query:) filter is served by Shopify's search index, which can omit a small number of real orders; the saved-run verification pass calls this to confirm or refute "missing in SHOPIFY" differences. A failed lookup returns ok=false with both id lists empty — it never classifies an order as missing.

parameter.name: shopifyAuthConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned ShopifyAuthConfig identifier.

parameter.name: orderIds
parameter.description: Shopify order ids to check; numeric ids or gid://shopify/Order/... values.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted run owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: connectTimeoutMillis
parameter.description: HTTP connect timeout for Shopify GraphQL requests.

parameter.name: readTimeoutMillis
parameter.description: HTTP read timeout for Shopify GraphQL requests.

parameter.name: maxAttempts
parameter.description: Maximum attempts for retryable Shopify GraphQL transport failures.

service.description: Enumerate exchanges created in Shopify whose return date falls inside the run window (product contract 2026-07-31: every Shopify exchange must have been imported into OMS). Sweeps updated_at with no upper bound and filters Return.createdAt client-side. Requires the read_returns scope. A failed sweep returns ok=false with an empty list — it never classifies anything.

Exchange-state point lookup for the exchange pair verify stage: per order, the returns containing exchange line items plus current totals, via nodes(ids:) with an Order fragment. Requires the token to carry the read_returns scope. A failed lookup returns ok=false with an empty map — it never classifies anything.

parameter.name: orderIds
parameter.description: Shopify order ids; numeric ids or gid://shopify/Order/... values.
